articles.title: Morning update
articles.description:
Morning update 

    
    

        
    
                Good morning Middle East Eye readers,

Here are the latest developments: 


	
	Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced that two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz. According to the statement, the separate incidents occurred after the vessels were attempting to pass through an "unauthorised route".
	
	
	South Korea's anti-piracy Cheonghae unit will expand its operations into waters nearby the Strait of Hormuz, according to a report by the Yonhap News Agency citing the Korean Defence Ministry. The government is set to submit a motion to parliament to extend the period of the unit's deployment to the region, which is expected to expire at the end of this year. 
	
	
	Israeli president Isaac Herzog warned prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu other senior officials of a "highly explosive and dangerous reality" in the West Bank amid increasing settler violence. Herzog said that the elections in Israel, the US and the Palestinian Authority - which the latter has since been postponed - alongside the olive harvest season are set to "create a highly explosive and dangerous reality".
	
	
	The US sanctioned two individuals and another entity accused of aiding Iran in sourcing man-portable air-defense systems (MANPADS). The statement said that sanctions "close off more of the channels Tehran uses to try to rebuild its arsenal and raise the risk for third-country brokers and suppliers".
	
	
	A ballistic missile attack which hit Hayfan in Yemen's Taiz governorate, killed four Yemenis from the same family, including three children, on Wednesday. Meanwhile, Houthi-affiliated media reported that Saudi-led coalition attacks over the past 24 hours have reportedly killed around 20 people across Yemen, including in the provinces of al-Jawf, al-Bayda, Saada, and Taiz.

"The countries of the region should know that, just as the Islamic Republic of Iran stands ready for battle with its finger on the trigger, it has also given the American side a powerful and rational response," Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said in a televised speech.

                US President Donald Trump said that Washington may need to "go after" a suspected underground nuclear complex in Iran, known as Pickaxe Mountain, if there is no deal reached.

"We might have to go after Pickaxe, we can do that in one hour, as soon as we want, at any time we want," Trump told Fox News.

Trump also did not rule out the possibility of resuming the war on Iran, saying: "It could happen if they don’t make a deal, but they want to make a deal very badly and there is a very good chance we make a deal."

"If I can make a deal, I would rather do it, [it would] save a lot of lives," he added.

articles.title: Iran says US ceasefire proposal 'insufficient' as strikes are reported on Qeshm Island
articles.description:
Iran says US ceasefire proposal 'insufficient' as strikes are reported on Qeshm Island 

    
    

          
      
      
        Submitted by 
MEE staff
 on 
Tue, 11/03/2026 - 15:59

        
      
    
      
    
                US officials said they launched 'defensive' strikes on Qeshm Island, the same day Trump vowed not to attack Iran
                      
                  
                  

  


                  A picture taken on 30 April 2023 shows a general view of the Iranian island of Qeshm (Atta Kenare/AFP)
                  Off
                  Iran cast doubt on the chances of a deal with the US on Tuesday, after the US carried out air strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island, with the fate of last-minute negotiations between the two sides uncertain.

The air strikes, which occurred late on Monday, came after US President Donald Trump said he did not plan to attack Iran after the midterm elections and voiced hope for a deal. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said an agreement could be reached and that the government was “authorised” to renew a truce.

However, on Tuesday, the head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Major General Mohsen Rezaei, rejected an offer passed to Tehran from Qatari negotiators.

“America’s response to the demands of the Iranian nation was insufficient. They must fully and explicitly address Iran's seven conditions and act upon them; only in this case will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened,” he said on X.

Last-minute negotiations to avert what officials and analysts in the region say could be a return to full-scale war took place against the backdrop of US air strikes on Qeshm Island, a strategic place that Iran has used as it attempts to assert control over the Strait of Hormuz.
  
    



  



The Wall Street Journal, which first reported the strikes on Qeshm, said the US was deliberately keeping the attacks quiet to reduce the risk of escalation. One US official described the strikes as “defensive” in the report.

According to the report, in one exchange, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired a surface-to-air missile at a US warplane, which fired back in self-defence. Another strike occurred after the US intercepted a missile fired from Qeshm at a commercial vessel. 

Iran also said it downed a US MQ-9 Reaper drone and two Lucas drones near the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. 


  

  Houthis launched cross border raids on Saudi military posts, sources say
    Read More »


Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said the ball was in Washington's court after Tehran had delivered what he described as a "strong and rational response” to the proposal conveyed by Qatar.

"The enemy seeks to force the Iranian nation into submission through threats and military action, but they are sorely mistaken; Iran will not submit," Qalibaf said.

Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said on Monday that Tehran has a seven-step proposal for a diplomatic solution that could be implemented in two days.

The plan would call for the US to end its blockade on Iranian ports, Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz waterway, a US waiver on Iranian oil sales, the cancellation of new sanctions on Iran, and then talks on the nuclear file.

The US and Iran agreed to a ceasefire in the spring and then signed a 14-point memorandum of understanding to advance talks, but it was never implemented. The talks collapsed in part over the US’s reluctance to agree to Iran controlling traffic in the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Morning update
articles.description:
Morning update

    
    

        
    
                Good morning Middle East Eye readers,

Here are the latest developments: 


	
	Iranian media is reporting that Tehran is not planning to attend talks with the United States, after President Donald Trump ordered US negotiators to travel to Pakistan on Monday, just days before a ceasefire in the Middle East expires.
	
	
	US President Donald Trump acknowledged that the war on Iran played a role in Republicans' losses in the midterm elections . "I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time people understood the importance of what I've done with Iran," he said during an interview with Fox News. In another interview with The New York Times, the American president said he was willing to accept the results of the midterm elections. 
	
	
	Iran's chief negotiator in talks with the US Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said that Americans voted "NO TO WAR" after Democrats routed Republicans in the midterm elections. "Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message," Ghalibaf wrote in a post on X.
	
	
	Iran’s  Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said four "rogue" oil tankers were destroyed after htting naval mines while trying to traverse a route in the Strait of Hormuz that is considered prohibited. The incident occurred south of the waterway, with the statement adding that IRGC forces also intercepted two other vessels.
	
	
	Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid has accused supporters of Benajmin Netanyahu's government of attempting to "crush" Tel Aviv's democracy. "What we are seeing tonight is an attempt to crush democracy and steal the election with the help of government plants in the security system," he said in a post on X. "This is a direct threat to our democracy from people who are unwilling to admit defeat," Lapid added.
	
	
	Speaking to the Financial Times, US President Donald Trump indicated that are no immediate plans to strike Iran. "I'm ready, we're ready. We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it," he said. "We seem to be getting everything we want," Trump added, referring to negotiations with Iran.

articles.title: JD Vance blames Iran war and support for Israel for failure in US mid-term elections
articles.description:
JD Vance blames Iran war and support for Israel for failure in US mid-term elections

    
    

          
      
      
        Submitted by 
MEE staff
 on 
Thu, 11/05/2026 - 10:22

        
      
    
      
    
                Vice president takes apparent swipe at Donald Trump's decision to go to war in the Middle East
                      
                  
                  

  


                  US President Donald Trump with Vice President JD Vance at the funeral service for US Senator Lindsey Graham in Washington, DC on 28 July 2026 (Alex Wroblewski/AFP)
                  Off
                  US Vice President JD Vance has blamed the war on Iran for the Republicans' brutal showing in the mid-term elections.

In an apparent swipe at President Donald Trump's Middle East strategy, Vance posted a lengthy social media post on Wednesday that also criticised US support for Israel.

“The reason we lost is the war,” Vance said, in the post on X.

He said that Republican voters had wanted Trump to focus on the cost of living and inflation, put "America first" and "change our relationship to Israel”, Vance wrote.

"If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest," he wrote.
  
    



  



"But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there."

With 54 seats in the US Senate and 237 in the House so far, the Democrats have swept to power and have the ability to seriously impede Trump's administration.

As the results poured in, Trump took to social media to distance himself from Republican candidates, despite campaigning heavily for them. 

"I wasn't on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE! Thank you for your attention to this matter," Trump wrote on X. 


One of the things the data analysts on our side obsessed over was "composition" – whether the electorate looked close enough to 2024 for Republicans to win. And despite polls that showed a Democrat blowout, the data kept on telling us the same story: in some states turnout was merely OK, in other states it was downright amazing, and in no state was it catastrophic. There was a genuine sense of optimism on our team: our people were showing up. So, I asked the smartest data guy I know, does that mean we're going to shock the world? "No," he told me. "We might do better than the polls suggest. But the data is telling us that a lot of Trump/Vance 2024 voters are pissed and planning to vote for the other guys. Our voters are turning out, but they may not vote for us." Well, that looks prophetic now. Our voters did show up. In Florida, for example, the electorate was 9 points more Republican than Democrat, just a couple points worse than 2024. Undoubtedly there were places we could have done better on turnout. But the main problem is not turnout. The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026. There will be a lot of infighting and arguing over what happened and why that is. One of the pollsters I really respect told me that our economic messaging wasn’t sharp enough down the stretch. I’m sure that’s true. But the real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone. Another pollster – one of the smartest people I know in politics, told me yesterday we’d lose the generic ballot by 13 points. I felt negative going into Tuesday, but even I was shocked by this. In his polling, he saw that a lot of Trump 2024 voters were angry and planning to vote for Democrats. He asked those voters who had abandoned us what would cause them to come back on our team. The top four answers, accounting for nearly all of the responses were: 1) End the war 2) Focus on cost of living/inflation 3) Put America First 4) Change our relationship to Israel. Our voters showed up. And the above four reasons are why many of them voted for Democrats. This is according to a pollster who nailed the results. While many spent Monday attacking Rachel Campos Duffy for calling for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, it turns out her political advice was sound. (She’s also a great person.) In the next few months, there's going to be a lot of gaslighting. Expect to hear any number of establishment politicians say the solution to our woes is amnesty. I'm open to the idea that we should change enforcement – by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labor, for instance. But anyone pushing amnesty is lying to you. The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night. If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there. I remain hopeful about our country. To the people who are pissed off and want to say, “I told you so”: you’re right, you did tell us so. Take that energy into electing Republicans who share your worldview. To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be. Let’s take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country.
— JD Vance (@JDVance) November 4, 2026


In an interview with the Wall Street Journal, Trump said that the Iran war was partially to blame for the Democrats' sweeping victory.

"Iran was a piece of it," he said. 

While Trump told Politico on Tuesday during election coverage that he didn't want to just "sit around there for two years vetoing everything", the 80-year-old billionaire, who is prohibited from running for a third term, may also feel unconstrained by lawmakers.

Under the Constitution, only Congress has the authority to declare war, but the last US president who sought congressional approval for the use of military force was George W Bush in 2001 and 2002.

articles.title: Israel's UN ambassador rejects Vance's claim that Iran war was behind midterm losses
articles.description:
Israel's UN ambassador rejects Vance's claim that Iran war was behind midterm losses

    
    

          
      
      
        Submitted by 
Nadav Rapaport
 on 
Thu, 11/05/2026 - 15:17

        
      
    
      
    
                'It’s very easy to always blame Israel for everything, but that is not the case,' says Danny Danon
                      
                  
                  

  


                  Danny Danon at the UN on 20 June 2025 (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images via AFP)
                  Off
                  Israel’s ambassador to the United Nations has rejected US Vice President JD Vance’s analysis that the war on Iran was the “real reason” the Republicans suffered sweeping losses in the midterm elections, and that the party should “change our relationship to Israel”.

“It’s very easy to always blame Israel for everything, but that is not the case,” Danny Danon told Israeli outlet i24 News.  

“I think it’s unfortunate that many made the link between rising prices, mainly oil prices, and the situation here in Israel,” the Israeli ambassador said. 

“The decision to attack Iran was the decision of the United States. It wasn’t our decision. We supported the US effort, and we think it was the right decision.”

The US and Israel attacked Iran at the end of February. The New York Times reported that in the weeks before the war began, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu shared intelligence with US President Donald Trump suggesting that the Iranian people would rise and topple their government in the event of an attack. 
  
    



  



No such regime change has occurred, and Iran has taken control of the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz, sending energy prices soaring.

The attendant rise in the cost of living in the US has been a key issue for American voters and one that Democrats have sought to exploit.

Vance takes to X

On Wednesday, after elections saw the Republicans lose both the Senate and the House of Representatives, Vance wrote in a lengthy post on X: “But the real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone… The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night.”  

“I think a part of it was Iran,” Trump has said in an interview, despite also saying that he “would have done it again”.

Vance also said in his post that polling had shown him that Trump voters wanted the US to “change our relationship to Israel”, as well as end the war on Iran, focus on the cost of living and “put America first”. 


  

  'I think a part of it was Iran': Trump acknowledges war's impact on midterm election losses
    Read More »


“If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next six years was worth it, then do so,” the vice president said, stating that “everyone knows why we lost”.

Danon said in his interview that Israel would “have to pay attention” to voices in both the Democratic and Republican parties that are critical of his country. “It will be harder for us,” the Israeli ambassador said, in relation to the increasing prominence of anti-Israel politicians in the US.

“We will always do whatever is necessary to protect ourselves,” said Danon, when questioned on a possible deal between the US and Iran following the election results.

In Israel, the losses have resulted in a wave of criticism of Netanyahu from politicians and commentators who believe the prime minister has become “toxic” for both Republicans and Democrats. 

Critics said that following the sweeping victory of the Democrats, Netanyahu can no longer lead Israel due to his unpopularity in the US.

One Israeli former diplomat maintained that the results in the US were the end of “an era of half a century in US-Israel relations”, adding that “what lies ahead is clouded in uncertainty”.

articles.title: Kirkland Lake Discoveries expands Mirado West gold zone beyond 1.1 kilometres
articles.description: Kirkland Lake Discoveries CEO Stefan Sklepowicz joined Steve Darling from Proactive to announce new diamond drilling results from four step-out holes at the Mirado West Zone, part of the company's KL South property in Kirkland Lake, Ontario. Sklepowicz told Proactive that the latest results have expanded the mineralized footprint of Mirado West to more than 1,100 metres of strike length, highlighting a system that hosts both high-grade gold veins and broad zones of bulk-tonnage mineralization. The drilling has intersected gold from less than 10 metres below surface to depths approaching 480 metres downhole, with the mineralized corridor remaining open in multiple directions. One of the standout results came from step-out hole KLM26-048, which intersected 10.53 grams per tonne gold over 9.20 metres, including a particularly high-grade interval of 31.93 g/t gold over 3.00 metres. The same hole also encountered a broad zone of bulk-tonnage mineralization at depth, returning 0.64 g/t gold over 68.00 metres, including a higher-grade section of 1.25 g/t gold over 26.50 metres. The company said the results demonstrate the potential for high-grade gold shoots to occur alongside wider, continuous zones of mineralization, providing opportunities to build both grade and potential resource volume. Additional step-out holes also returned repeated wide gold intervals, including zones measuring approximately 16 to 26 metres, supporting the company's interpretation that mineralization extends across a substantial corridor. Sklepowicz said the combination of high-grade intervals and broader mineralized zones is particularly encouraging, pointing to a system with the potential to host multiple styles of gold mineralization. Mirado West is located immediately adjacent to the Mirado South and Mirado North zones along the same structural trend. The expansion of Mirado West to more than 1.1 kilometres of strike length alongside Mirado South strengthens the company's view that these neighbouring zones could form part of a much larger, district-scale gold system. The company believes the broader corridor could contain multiple high-grade shoots surrounded by extensive mineralized envelopes, with the latest drilling providing further evidence of its potential scale. #proactiveinvestors #kirklandlakediscoveries #tsxv #kldc #otcqb #klklf #mining #Gold #GoldExploration #MiradoWest #KLSouth #KirklandLake #OntarioMining #HighGradeGold #GoldDrilling #MineralExploration #CanadianMining #JuniorMining

articles.title: Ameriwest advances Oregon copper-gold project with historic core resampling
articles.description: Ameriwest Critical Metals CEO David Watkinson joined Steve Darling from Proactive to discuss the company's efforts to advance the Bornite copper-gold-silver project in Oregon, including the reassessment of historic drill core, plans for an updated technical report and opportunities for additional exploration. Watkinson explained that the Bornite project was previously owned by Plexus Resources during the 1990s, when a pre-feasibility study and other technical work were completed. Ameriwest has since recovered a substantial portion of the historic drill core and transported it to Reno, Nevada, where the material is being logged and selected intervals resampled. The company has released results from the first three holes in a seven-hole resampling program. Watkins said the initial findings are generally consistent with historical results, with copper grades appearing somewhat higher and gold and silver values also showing improvements in several intervals. Additional assay results are expected as the remaining samples are processed, providing further information to compare against the original drilling data. The resampling initiative is designed to verify the historical exploration results and support the preparation of an updated technical report compliant with NI 43-101 standards. Ameriwest is targeting completion of that report in the first quarter of 2027. Alongside the technical work, the company is beginning the permitting process for additional confirmation drilling, which could take place next summer. A key focus is evaluating the potential of the project's breccia pipe deposit. Historical work identified a high-grade outer shell with grades exceeding 3% copper equivalent, while Ameriwest is also investigating whether the lower-grade interior portion of the structure could support economic mining under current metal price conditions. Watkinson said the company is undertaking technical studies to determine whether the interior of the breccia pipe could have mining potential, emphasizing that the work is intended to test that geological and economic concept. Ameriwest is also considering geophysical surveys to investigate whether additional breccia pipes may exist elsewhere in the area. The work could help identify extensions of the known mineralization at depth and investigate the possibility of a deeper feeder system. With historic core resampling underway, an updated technical report planned and permitting preparations beginning, Ameriwest is working to establish a clearer picture of the Bornite project's mineral potential and identify the next steps toward advancing the Oregon asset. #proactiveinvestors #ameriwestcriticalmetals #cse #awcm #otc #awlif #CopperExploration #GoldExploration #SilverExploration #BonnetProject #OregonMining #CriticalMetals #CopperMining #MineralExploration #MiningStocks #JuniorMining #NI43101

articles.title: Lightning Minerals' Warby tungsten targets advance toward maiden drilling
articles.description: Lightning Minerals Ltd managing director Troy Brice talked with Proactive about the completion of an expanded Phase 3 soil sampling program at the Warby Tungsten Project in North Queensland and the work now underway to refine targets for a maiden drill campaign. Brice said tungsten had emerged rapidly as an exploration focus at Warby after the company initially targeted gold at the project. The latest program comprised an additional 220 soil samples collected at 25-metre intervals along lines about 125 metres apart, adding greater detail to the company’s geological dataset. Brice also highlighted the discovery of further historical workings and visible wolframite during field activities. “Every time we go there, we find more, see more, it de-risks it for us, and we get more excited about the prospect,” he said. Lightning Minerals plans to combine the Phase 3 assay results with LiDAR surveying and petrological analysis being undertaken by the University of New South Wales. These datasets will help improve understanding of the controls on mineralisation and support the ranking of potential drill targets for 2027. He also provided an update on the company’s nearby gold exploration, where a Phase 2 drilling campaign was nearing completion, with assay results expected to provide the next important dataset. articles.title: 1911 Gold reports more underground drilling progress at True North ahead of potential 2027 restart
articles.description: 1911 Gold Corporation CEO Shaun Heinrichs joined Steve Darling from Proactive to discuss additional assay results from the company's ongoing underground infill and delineation drilling program at the True North Gold Project in Manitoba, where exploration is focused on strengthening mineral resources targeted for the early years of a potential mine restart. Heinrichs told Proactive that the latest drilling continues to support the company's work towards a potential restart decision in 2027. The program is designed to improve confidence in existing resources at the L10 Zone, which is accessible from Level 16, where underground development is advancing to provide access for planned test mining and bulk sampling activities in 2026 and 2027. The L10 Zone is situated at the intersection of the Shoreline Basalt unit and the regional east-west, steeply north-dipping L10 Shear Zone. Gold mineralization occurs in several vein styles, including generally northwest-trending extensional stockwork and breccia veins, as well as east-west-oriented, steeply north-dipping shear veins. The latest underground infill drilling was designed to evaluate the continuity of gold mineralization, confirm vein geometry and better understand grade distribution within the V-1020 and V-1010 veins. The company is also using the results to support the potential conversion of Inferred Mineral Resources to the Indicated category in areas identified for development and mining during the early years of the Preliminary Economic Assessment mine plan. Drilling was conducted on nominal 30-metre spacing, with the latest results covering 30 drill holes totalling 6,483 metres. All holes intersected the modelled veins, with every hole returning significant results except UG16-26-101. Heinrichs said preliminary overall results from the program were in line with expectations for the V-1020 vein, while results from the V-1010 vein were lower than anticipated. The company believes the ongoing work is an important part of reducing geologic al uncertainty and improving confidence in the mineral resources that would support an eventual return to production. #proactiveinvestors #1911goldcorporation #1911gold #tsxv #aumb #otcqx #aumbf #TrueNorthProject #Gold #GoldMining #ManitobaMining #GoldExploration #UndergroundDrilling #InfillDrilling #MineralResources #MineRestart #CanadianMining #JuniorMining

articles.description:
Turkey's parliament ratifies Mecca defence pact, clearing way for military support to Saudi Arabia

    
    

        
    
                Turkey's parliament on Thursday ratified the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, a defence pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey, clearing the way for Ankara to send military support to Riyadh amid attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis against the kingdom.

Under the agreement, signed by the three regional powers in August and sent to parliament for approval last month, an attack on one party constitutes an attack on all.

A ruling party lawmaker told Reuters last month that Turkey would also submit a mandate to parliament allowing military personnel to be deployed to Saudi Arabia under the pact.

articles.description:
Iran’s Khamenei says US election results will not end hostility towards Tehran

    
    

        
    
                Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei says Washington will continue its confrontation with Tehran despite the Democrats’ sweeping midterm victories.

In a message carried by state news agency IRNA, he rejected suggestions that “factional shifts” would “dissuade it from its hostility towards the Iranian nation”.

He said Washington seeks the “unconditional surrender of the Iranian nation”.

Referring to the US-Israeli war on Iran, Khamenei said the US had “suffered an irreversible decline” after a “self-made scandal”, adding that “the process of its collapse has accelerated”.

                Iran’s Defence Ministry spokesperson General Reza Talaeinik has portrayed the US midterm election results as further evidence that Trump and Netanyahu’s policies have failed.

Writing on social media, he called it an opportunity to “revisit the crimes of global arrogance, especially America, and to renew our pledge to resist interventionism”.

“Today, with the failure of Trump and Netanyahu’s warmongering policies becoming more apparent and the trend of their hegemony’s collapse in the world, the steadfastness of the Iranian nation is more than ever inspiring to free nations,” he wrote.

His comments follow a warning from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei that Tehran cannot trust Washington and that changes in US political leadership will not end its hostility towards Iran.

articles.description:
Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted a Houthi-fired missile in the Medina region

    
    

        
    
                The Saudi-led military coalition said on Thursday it had intercepted a missile fired by the Houthis towards the Medina region.

“Interception and destruction of a ballistic missile fired by the Houthi terrorist militia in the Medina region,” the coalition spokesman Colonel Turki Al-Malki said.

Earlier, Saudi Arabia's civil defence issued an alert for the Yanbu Governorate near the Red Sea in Medina province.

articles.title: Saudi coalition says it intercepted missile fired at Medina
articles.description:
Saudi coalition says it intercepted missile fired at Medina

    
    

        
    
                The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis on Thursday said it intercepted a ballistic missile fired by the group at the Medina region, home to one of Islam's holiest cities.

The announcement came just minutes after the kingdom's civil defence agency warned of potential danger in the area near the strategic port of Yanbu.

It was unclear if the two events were connected. 

"Air defence intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the Medina region," coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said in a post on X.

The Houthis rejected any suggestion they were targeting the city, saying such accusations were a "blatant and grave falsehood".

"Our operations target only its oil facilities and military bases," the group said in a statement.

articles.title: ‘It will crush us’: Israeli leaders in panic mode over fallout from US elections
articles.description:
‘It will crush us’: Israeli leaders in panic mode over fallout from US elections

    
    

        
    
                Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid warned after the US election results that Netanyahu’s continued leadership would endanger Israel’s security and deepen its international isolation.

"Israel cannot afford for him (Netanyahu), to remain prime minister. It endangers security, it endangers democracy, it will crush us in the world," Lapid wrote on X.

"The American election results in the morning have one unexpected outcome: they eliminate any possibility of a unity government led by Netanyahu," he added.

להתבטאויות של זיני בלילה ולתוצאות הבחירות באמריקה בבוקר יש תוצאה לא צפויה אחת: זה מחסל כל אפשרות לממשלת אחדות בראשות נתניהו. ישראל לא יכולה להרשות לעצמה שהוא יישאר ראש הממשלה. זה מסכן את הבטחון, זה מסכן את הדמוקרטיה, זה ירסק אותנו בעולם.— יאיר לפיד - Yair Lapid (@yairlapid) November 4, 2026 

Yair Golan, leader of the Democrats party, also sounded the alarm, warning that Netanyahu’s continued rule could push an already internationally isolated Israel towards “international sanctions, international isolation and a collision with the United States”.

תוצאות בחירות האמצע הלילה בארה״ב חושפות עד כמה נתניהו רעיל גם אצל הדמוקרטים וגם אצל הרפובליקנים. אני מתריע: המשך כהונתם של נתניהו ובן גביר עלול להוביל את ישראל למסלול של סנקציות בינלאומיות, בידוד בינלאומי ולהתנגשות עם ארה״ב, ידידתנו ובעלת בריתנו החשובה ביותר.ישראל זקוקה…— Yair Golan - יאיר גולן (@YairGolan1) November 4, 2026 

Jerusalem Post analyst Amichai Stein warned that the results could bring “harsher criticism of Israel, and less willingness to defend the traditional relationship between the two countries.”

His analysis warned that the success of candidates critical of Israel could influence the Democratic Party’s direction ahead of the 2028 presidential election.

עוד מכה לרפובליקנים (וגם לישראל):הדמוקרט טרוי ג'קסון מנצח במרוץ לסנאט האמריקאי במדינת מיין, ומביס את הרפובליקנית הפרו ישראלית סוזן קולינס לאחר 30 שנה— Amichai Stein (@AmichaiStein1) November 4, 2026 

Israel’s Channel 14 framed the Republican defeat as a direct setback for Israel, declaring in its headline: “A severe blow to Trump and Israel: Democrats won the midterm elections.”

articles.title: ‘Israel cannot afford to ignore’: Israeli press reels from Democratic sweep
articles.description:
‘Israel cannot afford to ignore’: Israeli press reels from Democratic sweep

    
    

        
    
                The Israeli press is taking stock of last night’s Democratic sweep of Congress, sounding the alarm over the consequences for Israel.

A Haaretz analysis this morning said Abdul El-Sayed’s victory over pro-Israel candidate Mike Rogers demonstrated “that even strident opposition to Israel is no barrier to winning competitive federal races.”

“El-Sayed won despite AIPAC spending more than $30 million to defeat him in the Democratic primary and another reported $9 million on behalf of Rogers in the general election,” it added.

The Jerusalem Post warned: “The implications of the US midterm elections for Israel could extend far beyond the loss of Republican control of Congress. The defeat comes amid broader shifts within the Democratic Party regarding Israel, the war with Iran, and the strategic relationship between Jerusalem and Washington.”

“One of the clearest takeaways from the election campaign is the political price the war with Iran has exacted on the Republican Party”, the analysis said, referring to the war Israel pushed the US into on 28 February.

“The expansion of the camp critical of Israel, and its growing access to positions of influence, represents a shift that Israel cannot afford to ignore,” it added.

articles.title: US election results fuel Israeli opposition's push to remove Netanyahu
articles.description:
US election results fuel Israeli opposition's push to remove Netanyahu

    
    

        
    
                As news emerged on Wednesday that the Democratic Party had won a landslide victory, regaining control of the US Congress, Israeli politicians, journalists and experts warned of the results' grave implications for Israel's national security, pointing to the declining standing of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the US.

Former Israeli prime minister Yair Lapid, who was re-elected to parliament last week as part of the centre-right Together alliance, said the US election results had "eliminated" any possibility of forming a unity government with Netanyahu.

"Israel cannot afford for him to remain prime minister. It endangers security, it endangers democracy, it will crush us in the world," Lapid said on X on Wednesday morning.

Recent Israeli reports indicated that US President Donald Trump is applying pressure on Netanyahu and the Israeli opposition leaders to form a unity government that will exclude extremists in order to advance his Middle Eastern policies.

Yair Golan, leader of the left-wing Democrats alliance, also described Netanyahu as a threat to Israel's security in the wake of the US election results, which saw progressive Democrats, including Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed – the first Muslim elected to the US Senate – win races across the country.

Read more: US election results fuel Israeli opposition's push to remove Netanyahu

                  As news emerged on Wednesday that the Democratic Party had won a landslide victory, regaining control of the US Congress, Israeli politicians, journalists and experts warned of the results' grave implications for Israel's national security, pointing to the declining standing of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the US.

Former Israeli prime minister Yair Lapid, who was re-elected to parliament last week as part of the centre-right Together alliance, said the US election results had "eliminated" any possibility of forming a unity government with Netanyahu.

"Israel cannot afford for him to remain prime minister. It endangers security, it endangers democracy, it will crush us in the world," Lapid said on X on Wednesday morning.

Recent Israeli reports indicated that US President Donald Trump is applying pressure on Netanyahu and the Israeli opposition leaders to form a unity government that will exclude extremists in order to advance his Middle Eastern policies.

Yair Golan, leader of the left-wing Democrats alliance, also described Netanyahu as a threat to Israel's security in the wake of the US election results, which saw progressive Democrats, including Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed – the first Muslim elected to the US Senate – win races across the country.
  
    



  



Golan said Netanyahu has become "toxic" in the US, both within the Democratic party and the Republican party, adding that if the Israeli prime minister continues to rule it could "lead Israel onto a path of international sanctions, international isolation, and a collision with the United States".


'Netanyahu’s continued tenure is an immediate danger to our special relationship with the United States'

- Amir Tibon, Haaretz


According to Golan, the most left-leaning leader of the Zionist Israeli opposition, Israel is now facing a choice between a "boycotted, backward, and isolated" country led by Netanyahu, or "a strong, advanced, free, and secure Israel".

"Netanyahu lost the elections. He is dangerous to Israel," Golan said on X, adding "we have no time to waste. We must form a change government now."

The Democrats MP Gilad Kariv echoed the position of his party leader on Wednesday, ruling out a unity government with Netanyahu's Likud party.

Kariv said on X that "anyone who is still talking this morning about unity with Netanyahu does not understand the results of the elections in Israel and does not understand the results of the elections in the United States."

'US-Israel relations comes to an end'

Progressive US Democrats like Sayed, who have been calling for an end to military aid to Israel over its genocide in Gaza, are viewed by Israeli US affairs experts and journalists as a threat to Israel's very existence.

On Wednesday, former Israeli foreign minister Tzipi Livni, a fierce critic of Netanyahu, said that the prime minister can no longer "preserve the legitimacy of the existence of the state of the Jewish people, or our right to defend ourselves, in the face of the views of some of the newly elected officials".


'An era of half a century in US-Israel relations, as we have known it, comes to an end'

- Michael Oren, former Israeli diplomat


Gili Cohen, the diplomatic correspondent of Israel's Kan 11, said the US electoral results are "not only a defeat for President Donald Trump, but also for Israel’s standing" in the US, as the much-needed American military aid is now on the balance.

Amir Tibon, a journalist at the Israeli left-wing newspaper Haaretz, described the election results as "a political earthquake" with grave consequences for Israel.

"Netanyahu’s continued tenure is an immediate danger to our special relationship with the United States," he wrote on X, adding that the prime minister had become "toxic" not only within the Democratic Party but also among Republicans, some of whose leaders are now blaming him for their defeat.

On Wednesday, Trump acknowledged that the US-Israel war on Iran, launched in February under pressure from Netanyahu, played a role in his party's defeat.

"If Israel wants to start rebuilding its very poor standing in the US, it must part ways with Netanyahu," Tibon said, adding that a failure to do so could lead "to very dangerous places".


  

  Aipac and the Michigan Senate race: How the Israel lobby became toxic
    Read More »


The Democrats' landslide victory also raised concerns among right-wing Israeli politicians and commentators.

Journalist Ariel Kahana told Radio 103FM that "Israel suffered a very serious blow" on Tuesday's elections, as Israel "was on the ballot".

"Netanyahu is a burden on Israel," Kahana said.

Political analyst Kobby Barda of the Jewish People Policy Institute think tank said that Iran was the "big winner" of the US elections, while Netanyahu was the "huge loser".

"The face of Israel’s government can’t be Netanyahu anymore," right-winger Barda said, citing his unpopularity rates in the US.

Michael Oren, a former Israeli diplomat, warned that the triumphs of people like Sayed, who he called "a venomously anti-Israel candidate" and "antisemitic", could lead to catastrophic ramifications for Israel.

Oren warned that "the halt of military aid may be only the beginning", saying that intelligence and military systems sharing with the US, entry visas for Israelis and supplies of essential military components were all now at risk. He added that US sanctions against Israel were also a possibility.

"Thus, an era of half a century in US-Israel relations, as we have known it, comes to an end," Oren said, adding that "what lies ahead is clouded in uncertainty".

articles.description:
Netanyahu says 'serious suspicions' of foreign interference in vote

    
    

        
    
                Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday that there are "serious suspicions" of foriegn interference in the Israeli elections after his Likud party suffered resounding defeats in the recent vote. 

"There are serious suspicions that foreign states have spent considerable sums to influence the outcome of the elections in Israel," Netanyahu said in a video posted on social media.

He blamed "extremist Islam" for "tearing apart countries in Europe", adding that this "challenge" cannot be confronted by "a government dependent on extremist Islam and these Islamist parties, which deny the very existence of a Jewish state".

This comes as Israel's President Isaac Herzog begins consultations with party leaders to form the next government.


אזרחי ישראל היקרים, האסלאם הקיצוני הוא האתגר שמפרק היום מדינות באירופה. זהו האתגר שמאיים גם עלינו. הוא מאיים מבחוץ על ידי איראן וגרורותיה, ומבית על ידי מפלגות אסלאמיסטיות של תומכי טרור. הם חותרים למחוק את הזהות היהודית של מדינת ישראל. הם אומרים זאת בגלוי. הם חותרים למנוע מאיתנו את היכולת להגן על עצמנו מפני אויבינו. ואני שואל שאלה פשוטה: מי יוכל להתמודד עם האתגר הזה? מי שבוודאות לא תוכל להתמודד עם האיום של האסלאם הקיצוני היא ממשלה שתלויה באסלאם הקיצוני ובמפלגות האסלאמיסטיות הללו, ששוללות את עצם קיומה של מדינה יהודית. צריך רק להקשיב למה שנציגיהן אומרים. הם אומרים את זה בגלוי. הם אומרים: “זה כבוד להיות שהיד, זה הכבוד הנשגב ביותר”. “חמאס הוא ארגון צדקה”. והם מקדישים את ההישגים שלהם בקלפי למחבלי הנוח’בה הנתעבים שיושבים אצלנו בכלא. לא רק שממשלה כזאת לא תילחם באויבינו, היא פשוט תפרק אותנו מבפנים. זה בנפשנו. אבל יש ממשלה שכן יכולה להתמודד עם האתגר הזה. ממשלה לאומית רחבה בראשות הליכוד, בהנהגתי, שתכלול את כל מרכיבי הגוש הלאומי ואת כל המפלגות הציוניות שירצו להצטרף. אמרתי את זה במהלך מערכת הבחירות וחזרתי על זה רק לפני יומיים. מה שכל כך ברור לכם, לרוב המוחלט של אזרחי ישראל, נדחק הצידה כלאחר יד על ידי ראשי גוש השמאל. הם עוסקים בהקמת ממשלת מיעוט צרה, ממשלה שנשענת על תומכי הטרור הללו, והם מכריזים מעל כל במה על תנאים בלתי אפשריים שנועדו לסכל מראש כל אפשרות להקים ממשלה לאומית רחבה. הם מעדיפים את האינטרס הפוליטי שלהם על האינטרס הלאומי. ואתם יודעים, ואתם מסכימים גם עם דבר נוסף. מוכרחים להגיע לאמת. ישנם חשדות חמורים למעורבות של מדינות זרות בכסף עצום להטיית תוצאות הבחירות במדינת ישראל. יושב ראש ועדת הבחירות, השופט סולברג, הנחה את השב”כ לפתוח בחקירה ביטחונית. הוא קבע שיש להסיר את כל החסמים בפני החקירה הזו. הוא צודק. חייבים להגיע לאמת במלואה, ללא טיוח וללא דיחוי. טוהר הבחירות הוא יסוד הדמוקרטיה. חייבים לשמור עליו וחייבים לשמור על המדינה שלנו.

articles.description:
Herzog warns Netanyahu of 'highly explosive and dangerous reality' amid rising settler violence

    
    

        
    
                Israeli president Isaac Herzog warned prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu other senior officials of a "highly explosive and dangerous reality" in the West Bank amid increasing settler violence.

"The IDF commanders, the police officers and the Shin Bet personnel present a worrying picture of limited tools and a shortage of manpower," Herzog wrote in the letter sent to Netanyahu, defence minister Israel Katz, the Israeli army chief of staff Eyal Zamir and attorney general Gali Baharav-Miara.

Herzog said that the elections in Israel, the US and the Palestinian Authority - which the latter has since been postponed - alongside the olive harvest season are set to "create a highly explosive and dangerous reality".

"A severe flare-up on the ground is liable to carry severe and far-reaching consequences, both for Israel’s security and its functioning as a sovereign state, and for Israel’s international standing, Diaspora Jewry, the Israeli economy, and more," the Israeli president further warned.

He added that there is a "moral disgrace and the stain on us" when innocent Palestinians are harmed, and stressed that "there is no room for this lawlessness in a sovereign state".

articles.description:

                Vast majority of Jewish voters in US want sanctions against 'violent West Bank settlers' 
                      
                  
                  

  


                  Voting booths at a polling location in Manchester, New Hampshire, are ready for voters, on 8 September 2026 (CJ Gunther/Getty Images/AFP)
                  Off
                  A supermajority of Jewish Americans think Israel and the American Israel Public Affairs Committee’s (Aipac) actions are increasing antisemitism in the US, according to a new poll.

The poll commissioned by J Street, a US-based pro-Israel think tank, shows a deep gap between how Jewish American voters view organisations like Aipac and Israel’s occupation of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, compared to how the state of Israel and its allies in the US portray antisemitism.

The poll says 66 percent of Jewish voters in the US believe that Aipac’s campaign spending against candidates who criticise Israel actually increases antisemitism in the country.

In addition, 60 percent believe that Jewish organisations that label harsh criticism of Israel as antisemitic are exploiting concerns about antisemitism to defend unpopular Israeli government policies.

Notably, 80 percent of Jewish voters believe that Israel’s actions in the occupied West Bank and Gaza are increasing antisemitism in the US.
  
    



  



“Conventional wisdom about the impact of Jewish concerns over antisemitism and what it means to support Israel often misses the mark on how Jews process these issues in America’s political context,” Jim Gerstein, founding partner at GBAO Strategies, which conducted the poll between 28 October and 3 November, said.

“The reality is that Jews express nuanced thinking on these issues that is frequently missing in the extensive media coverage of the Jewish community,” he added.

The US midterm elections marked a sweeping Democratic victory where the US war on Iran and US support for Israel played a central role in races such as Michigan.

Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed won the race there in a historic landslide against Aipac supported Republican candidate Mike Rogers. 


  

  Aipac spent $55m on losing congressional candidates in midterm elections: Report
    Read More »


Sayed, who campaigned on cutting US aid to Israel along with other Middle Eastern countries and condemned Israel’s genocide on Gaza, won 60 percent of early Jewish voters, according to a poll by Mercury Public Affairs.

The poll also showed that New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who has been smeared as being an antisemite, had a higher favorability rating among Jewish Americans, 49 percent, compared to outgoing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, at 20 percent.

Overall, the poll from GBAO Strategies found that 72 percent of Jewish voters supported Democratic candidates and that 76 percent supported sanctions against “violent West Bank settlers”.

The president of J Street said the poll underscored the falsehood of stereotypes about Jewish voters in the US.

“Jewish Americans have been treated as a political football throughout this election cycle, with politicians and commentators insisting that our community demands unconditional support for the Israeli government. These results tell a very different story,” Jeremy Ben-Ami said.

“Jewish voters overwhelmingly backed Democrats, strongly oppose President Trump and support holding the Israeli government accountable for its actions. They want American leadership that advances peace and security for Israelis and Palestinians, and they are rejecting the idea that supporting Israel means writing its government a blank check,” he added.

articles.title: Israeli president Herzog deliberates after Eisenkot receives majority Knesset backing to become prime minister
articles.description:
Israeli president Herzog deliberates after Eisenkot receives majority Knesset backing to become prime minister

    
    

        
    
                Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot has received the backing of a majority of Knesset members to be prime minister, possibly granting him the mandate to attempt to form the next government.

Eisenkot received 67 recommendations compared with 46 for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The Yashar party urged Israeli president Isaac Herzog on Thursday to hand Eisenkot the mandate to form the next government "as soon as possible", adding that its the largest number of recommendations given to a candidate for forming a government since 2015.

"Benjamin Netanyahu is a caretaker prime minister leading a minority of just 46 seats," the party said. "He has no mandate, no majority and no public trust."

While Herzog expressed that the result was "clear", he indicated that he would hold further talks with party leaders to clarify the situation before assigning the mandate to form a government on Sunday.

articles.title: Joint List says it will back Eisenkot to form Israel’s next government
articles.description: Arab-led parties won a record 19 seats in Israel's 120-seat parliament in last week's general election.

articles.title: Arab-led Joint List says it will back Eisenkot to form Israel's next government
articles.description:
Arab-led Joint List says it will back Eisenkot to form Israel's next government

    
    

          
      
      
        Submitted by 
MEE staff
 on 
Thu, 11/05/2026 - 15:25

        
      
    
      
    
                Alliance’s endorsement gives opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the backing of 67 lawmakers in the 120-seat Knesset
                      
                  
                  

  


                  Yousef Jabareen (centre), leader of Israel's Arab-led Joint List political alliance, celebrates as the first exit polls are announced during Israel's election last week (Ahmad Gharabli/AFP)
                  Off
                  The Arab-led Joint List has said it will back Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a new government, dealing a heavy blow to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's efforts to remain in power.

The Joint List announced on Thursday that it would "recommend that Gadi Eisenkot be tasked with forming the government", bringing the total number of lawmakers backing him to 67 in the 120-seat Knesset.

The decision follows Wednesday's endorsement by Ra'am, another Arab-led party, whose eight lawmakers also backed Eisenkot.

The two parties together secured a record 19 seats in last week's general election, giving them a potentially decisive role in determining who forms Israel's next government.

Netanyahu's right-wing bloc won 53 seats in the 27 October election, while the opposition alliance led by Eisenkot secured 48. A majority in parliament requires 61 seats.
  
    



  



The results left both camps short of the numbers needed to govern independently, making the support of Arab-led parties and smaller political factions crucial to the coalition negotiations.

The Joint List said its unanimous decision reflected public demands to prevent Netanyahu and his government from returning to power.

It also said the endorsement was intended to widen the gap between Eisenkot and Netanyahu and strengthen the chances of replacing the incumbent government.

The alliance, which comprises three Arab-led factions, said its decision came despite the opposition's failure to sufficiently challenge Netanyahu's political direction, incitement against Arab citizens and attempts to undermine the legitimacy of their electoral choices.

However, the endorsements do not necessarily mean the Arab parties will join an Eisenkot-led government.


  

  How an election defeat triggered a carnival of racism against Palestinians
    Read More »


The Joint List has said it is prepared to support an opposition government from outside the governing coalition, rather than take ministerial positions.

Its leaders have opposed joining a government while Israel continues its occupation of Palestinian territory.

Eisenkot and his opposition partners have also faced divisions over cooperation with Arab-led parties. 

The opposition bloc has set conditions for potential partners, including recognising Israel as a Jewish state, supporting military conscription and condemning Hamas.

Some opposition figures have rejected relying on Arab lawmakers, while others have argued that their support is essential to ending Netanyahu's rule.

Eisenkot, 66, has repeatedly rejected the idea of a Palestinian state alongside Israel.

While serving as army chief between 2015 and 2019, he publicly advocated for closer ties with Saudi Arabia, saying the two countries should work together to counter Iran's influence in the region.

He also said Israel would be willing to share intelligence with Riyadh to confront Tehran.

articles.description:
Iran’s Basij chief praises 'resistance cinema', saying that 'change has begun' in US, Israel

    
    

        
    
                Iran’s Basij commander Hossein Taeb has said that the US and Israel are seeing change amid their ongoing attempts at transforming the Middle East's landscape.

"Today, we say that change has begun in America and Israel, and we will soon see it across different areas," he said during the closing ceremony of the 19th International Resistance Film Festival in Tehran.

His highlighted the use of media and film as a way of "disrupting America’s media monopoly", describing it as "resistance cinema".

"The staging of this festival under such circumstances signifies that - much like a combatant who never abandons their launchers during military defence - an artist engaged in the 'perceptual battlefield' does not desert their post, even under the shadow of war, economic siege, or any other threat," he said.

"Through their portrayal of the Resistance, they inflict a new defeat upon the enemy."

Referencing US-Israeli attacks on Gaza, Lebanon, Iraq and Syria, Taeb said: "All these crimes took place; children were killed, and the oppressed peoples of the region suffered. Yet, the true losers in this conflict were the United States and Israel."

articles.description:
Israeli settlers seize eight homes in occupied West Bank village west of Jericho

    
    

        
    
                Israeli settlers seized eight Palestinian homes on Wednesday in the village of al-Duyuk al-Tahta, west of Jericho, in the occupied West Bank, Wafa news reported.

Palestinian security sources told Wafa that the settlers, accompanied by their families, stormed the eight homes, which were empty at the time of the raid, and smashed their doors, remaining inside the property.

Israeli forces also stormed Jericho and its refugee camps on Wednesday evening, deploying military vehicles along the city’s streets, according to Wafa.

They also reported that Israeli soldiers raided the area surrounding the Thabet Thabet Governmental Hospital in Tulkarm, in the occupied West Bank, and ransacked the home of Mohammed Ibrahim Shahada, secretary of Fatah in Tulkarm refugee camp on Wednesday.

articles.title: Israeli forces demolish five West Bank buildings and displace over 100 Palestinians
articles.description:
Israeli forces demolish five West Bank buildings and displace over 100 Palestinians

    
    

          
      
      
        Submitted by 
Mohammed Turkman
 on 
Thu, 11/05/2026 - 12:24

        
      
    
      
    
                Residents of Biddu say troops gave them no warning before razing their homes, as Palestinian officials report a sharp rise in demolitions across Jerusalem and its suburbs
                      
                  
                  

  


                  A Palestinian man stands amid the rubble of five residential buildings demolished by Israeli forces in Biddu, occupied West Bank, on 5 November 2026 (Mohammed Turkman/MEE)
                  Off
                  Israeli forces demolished five Palestinian residential buildings in the occupied West Bank on Thursday without warning, displacing more than 100 people.

Troops raided the town of Biddu, northwest of Jerusalem, in the early morning, forcing residents of 12 apartments out before demolishing them.

Residents said soldiers fired stun grenades and tear gas at homeowners, preventing them from retrieving their belongings before the demolitions began.

Ahmad Abu Eid, the owner of one of the homes, said Israeli forces raided the town without warning and began demolishing the buildings. He said the properties belonged to him, his sons and his daughter.

Soldiers prevented the family from removing the contents of their homes and gave them insufficient time to evacuate. As a result, they lost access to their furniture, clothes and personal belongings.
  
    



  



Abu Eid's son, Salman, was a former prisoner released under last year's prisoner exchange deal and deported to Egypt. Abu Eid believes the demolitions were an act of retaliation linked to his son's release.

"What has happened to us is what happens to all Palestinians. We have no other land, and we will endure whatever they do to us," he told Middle East Eye.

Israeli soldiers cited the absence of building permits as the reason for the demolitions. The homes were located in Area C of the occupied West Bank.


  

  New ‘Nakba’ in Jerusalem: Israel steps up Silwan demolitions near Al-Aqsa
    Read More »


The West Bank was divided into Areas A, B and C under the 1995 Oslo agreement. Area A falls under the Palestinian Authority's administrative and security control, while Area B is under PA administrative control and Israeli security control. Area C remains under Israeli administrative and security control. 

Israeli forces frequently demolish Palestinian homes and other structures across the West Bank, citing the lack of building permits, particularly in Area C. However, Palestinians are almost never granted the permits required to build legally.

The PA’s Jerusalem Governorate office described the demolitions and displacement as a dangerous escalation aimed at undermining the Palestinian presence on the outskirts of Jerusalem, and a violation of international law.

It warned of the consequences for Palestinian families, many of whom have been displaced and deprived of their homes.

Uptick in Jerusalem demolitions

Salem Abu Eid, a member of Biddu municipal council, said that two of the demolished homes were not subject to judicial demolition orders, despite legal challenges filed with Israeli courts.

He told MEE the demolitions affected a residential complex housing nine Palestinian families.

According to Abu Eid, Israeli authorities had previously issued stop-construction notices, rather than demolition orders, for more than 20 homes in the town.

He said homeowners had filed objections with the Israeli Civil Administration in Beit El, with several lawyers currently handling the cases.

"The last demolition in the town took place several months ago, targeting a structure built of wood and tile, alongside the bulldozing of what is known as the municipal park," he added.

  
  
      



    Israeli bulldozers arrived early in the morning without warning, forcing residents from their homes without sufficient time to retrieve their belongings (Mohammed Turkman/MEE)
  






  
    



  









Abu Eid said Israel justifies the demolitions by citing the absence of building permits, claiming the properties are located in Area C or near the separation wall. However, he pointed out that the nearest of the targeted homes is about 700 metres from the wall.

He called for greater support for affected families, stronger Palestinian solidarity, and assistance for those who had lost their homes.

"We urge official authorities to compensate the families for their lost homes and property, and to assist in providing alternative housing or constructing new homes for them even if in different locations," said Eid.

The Jerusalem Governorate office has recorded a significant increase in demolitions and land-clearing operations in Jerusalem and its surrounding areas this year.
  
    



  



During the first nine months of 2026, it documented 427 operations, including 66 cases of forced self-demolition, in which Palestinians were compelled to tear down their own homes; 294 demolitions carried out using Israeli machinery; and 32 land-levelling operations.

In October alone, the office recorded a further 44 demolition and land-levelling operations, bringing the total number documented between January and the end of October to 471.

The figures cover homes, other structures and land, and are not limited to residential properties.

articles.title: Israeli settlers move into homes near West Bank city
articles.description:
Israeli settlers move into homes near West Bank city

    
    

        
    
                Israeli settlers moved into houses they say they purchased legally near the occupied West Bank city of Jericho this week, while Palestinian officials say the sale documents were forged.

An AFP reporter saw families with children moving into homes on the outskirts of the ancient city in the West Bank.

Palestinians fear that the new settlement outpost could bring an increased army presence and settler violence.

Several Palestinian communities in the greater Jericho area have already been driven from their homes by harassment from settlers over the past year.

The Israeli families moved into eight houses just outside Jericho's city limits on Wednesday, Hanan Greenwood, a settler representative, told AFP, near the ancient site known as the Hasmonean Palaces.

Hussein Hamayel, governor of the Jericho region, told AFP that the land in question is owned by the Palestinian Authority and cannot be sold.

"What is being promoted is a forgery, not a sale, and what is being circulated is settler propaganda," Hamayel said.

articles.title: Gaza: Indiscriminate Israeli gunfire kills and terrorises displaced families
articles.description:
Gaza: Indiscriminate Israeli gunfire kills and terrorises displaced families

    
    

          
      
      
        Submitted by 
Abdallah al-Naami
 on 
Mon, 11/02/2026 - 13:47

        
      
    
      
    
                From children playing out to families queuing for food, indiscriminate Israeli shooting has made daily life a struggle for survival across Gaza
                      
                  
                  

  


                  Safia Abo Amra hold a photo of her granddaughter Fatima al-Bayouk, who was killed by Israeli gunfire earlier this month (Abdallah al-Naami/MEE)
                  Off
                  After finishing her homework, Fatima al-Bayouk went to play with her cousins outside her grandmother’s home in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza, when an Israeli bullet struck her neck.

Moments later, the eight-year-old Palestinian girl returned home trembling, blood soaking her shirt. She screamed that her cousin had been shot, unaware that she had been hit herself.

The bullet had lodged in her lung. After a week in hospital, she died from her injuries.

For her grandmother, Safia Abo Amra, Bayouk - the sole survivor of her immediate family in an earlier Israeli air strike - was far more than a granddaughter. She had become her closest companion and the centre of her life.

“Fatima was my best friend. We did everything together, cooking, going on walks; we even slept on the same mattress. I have seven sons and six daughters, yet Fatima was more precious to me than all of them,” Abo Amra told Middle East Eye.
  
    



  



Despite everything she had endured, Bayouk had brought joy back into her grandmother’s life. Her uncle Ahmad Abo Amra remembered her as a bright, cheerful girl whose smile lifted the spirits of those around her.


'My life was attached to Fatima’s. I wish I could die after her'

- Safia Abo Amra, Palestinian grandmother 


“The best thing about Fatima was her smile that always brought joy to everyone around her. She was smart, responsible and loved happy occasions like weddings and family gatherings,” he said.

Her death reflects a wider pattern of indiscriminate Israeli gunfire that has become a daily threat to Palestinians across the Gaza Strip, particularly displaced families living near the so-called Yellow Line.

Israeli shooting from military positions, tanks and quadcopter drones has killed and wounded hundreds of civilians since the October 2025 ceasefire. It has also disrupted access to basic necessities and made everyday activities dangerous.

As Israel expands its control over more of the territory, families increasingly find themselves exposed to gunfire, with little protection and few places to seek safety.

A life cut short

For Bayouk’s family, her death was particularly devastating. She had already survived the loss of her immediate family in the early days of Israel’s genocide.

On 13 December 2023, an Israeli air strike targeted their home in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, killing her family. Bayouk survived and went to live with her grandmother in Deir al-Balah, where Abo Amra and other relatives tried to rebuild her life amid the devastation of the war.


'With her beautiful soul, she was the one to help me through my grief for my daughter and grandchildren'

- Safia  Abo Amro


“We did our best to provide everything Fatima needed and make her feel cared for and surrounded by people who love her,” Abo Amra said.

“I wanted to make up for the loss of her family, but with her beautiful soul, she was the one to help me through my grief for my daughter and grandchildren.”

Education remained an important part of Bayouk’s life as she grew up in her grandmother’s home. Concerned for her safety, Abo Amra refused to send her to a UN school after hearing that Israeli stray bullets frequently reached the area. Instead, she paid monthly fees to enrol her in a local school.

“I walked Fatima to school every day. She was very smart and always did her homework before playing,” Abo Amra said.

Her death reopened the grandmother’s wounds.

“I was shocked and couldn't speak or move. Her death was twice as painful for me; it reminded me of my daughter and grandchildren who were killed at the beginning of the war,” Abo Amra said. 

“My life was attached to Fatima’s. I wish I could die after her.”

  
  
      



    Fatima al-Bayouk liked to dress well, her family says (Abdallah al-Naami/MEE)
  









Despite her young age, Bayouk left a lasting impression on those around her. She loved dressing up, particularly for family celebrations.

Her uncle Reda Abo Amra remembered how much she enjoyed choosing new clothes. The family had recently bought her winter clothes, but she never got the chance to wear them.

“She always liked to be well-dressed. We bought her new clothes for winter, but she was killed before she could wear them,” he told MEE.
  
    



  



Bayouk was not the first member of her family to be killed by Israeli gunfire. Six months before her death, her uncle Masoud Abo Amra, who was born with a mental disability, was shot in the neck while visiting his sister in Khan Younis.

“Masoud was Fatima's favourite uncle. She was devastated when she bid him farewell,” Ahmad said.

‘When the shooting starts, life stops’

For displaced families in Gaza, Israeli gunfire is not only a deadly threat but also a constant disruption to daily life.

Zaid al-Kafarna, 19, and his family of 10 were displaced from northern Gaza to the Um Duhair area, south of Deir al-Balah, days before the October 2025 ceasefire came into effect.

Kafarna said Israeli shooting was initially “occasional” and took place some distance from their tents. But it gradually became more frequent and moved closer to the camp. Over the past three months, he said, it had become a daily threat, frequently causing deaths, injuries and damage. 


  

  Gaza family mourns boys killed by Israel along Yellow Line
    Read More »


“I miraculously survived stray bullets several times. My friend and neighbour, Mohammad Aqel, was killed a few weeks ago by a stray bullet while he was preparing to return to northern Gaza,” Kafarna told MEE.

His mother, Shereen al-Kafarna, was recently wounded by an Israeli bullet while inside their tent. She described how the shooting brings life in the camp to a standstill.

“When the shooting starts, life stops in our camp. Neighbours warn each other. We leave everything and hold the children, then lie on the ground to avoid the bullets hitting around us. Everyone is terrified, especially the children,” she said.

The gunfire also disrupts Palestinians' efforts to secure basic necessities, including food and water.

“Sometimes while we are waiting in queues for water and food, Israeli tanks and quadcopter drones start shooting directly towards us,” Zaid said.

“Everyone panics. We lie on the ground at the side of the road, watching the aid trucks carrying our food and water drive away to escape the bullets. On those days, we don't have anything to eat or drink.” 

Nowhere to go

The pattern of daily Israeli shootings near the Yellow Line, alongside the ongoing expansion of Israel’s buffer zone in Gaza, raised questions among families about whether the gunfire is as random as it appears.

Many believe that the shootings appear to form part of a military tactic to force Palestinian families out of their homes and tents, allowing Israel to expand its control over more territory through force.
  
    



  



In the year following the ceasefire, Israeli control over Gaza grew from 53 to 70 percent, reflecting what the Palestinians describe as a systematic policy of territorial expansion.

Families living near the Yellow Line said the threat of stray bullets had forced several others to leave their camps.

“Watching families leave our camp every day makes us feel even more afraid. We wish we could move away from the bullets, but we have nowhere to go,” Shereen told MEE. 

“Even if we had somewhere to go, we can't afford the extremely expensive cost of transportation.”

With few options for escape, some families have resorted to building small sand barriers and digging trench-like holes inside and between their tents to shelter from the bullets.

  
  
      



    Shadi Siam dug a trench for his family next to their tent to take cover from Israeli gunfire (Abdallah al-Naami/MEE)
  











Next to his tent, Shadi Siam dug a small trench to protect his family of five.

“I fear for my children's lives every time I hear Israeli stray bullets flying low,” Siam told MEE.

“My children wake up terrified, and I carry them to the hole where we all hide for two to five hours until the shooting stops,” he added.

“I don't know how I will protect them when the winter comes, and the hole becomes unusable.”
